page: Microsoft Azure D32a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 family, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7452 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz, providing 32 dedicated virtual CPUs distributed over 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system is provisioned with 128 GB of main memory, maintaining a 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 859 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while dedicated GPU hardware accelerators are absent.

Performance profiles demonstrate high memory throughput and dependable single-threaded computational power. Synthetic tests record a stress-ng single-core rating of 2707.98, placing it within the top 25 percent of tested systems, while multi-core metrics place in the median range. In PassMark memory testing, the instance achieved 2984.77, placing it in the top 10 percent for memory bus capability. For operational benchmarks, the platform delivers 26.26 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 11.64 GB per second of static web serving bandwidth. Inference on small language models (135M) generates 323.62 tokens per second, but throughput drops significantly on larger architectures.

Hardware tradeoffs center on instruction support and storage configuration. The AMD EPYC processor supports standard AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instructions but lacks AVX-512 extensions and AMX units, which constrains vectorized scientific computing and intensive deep learning inference. The included 859 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space, balancing storage performance without separate disk attachments. Given these characteristics, the D32a_v4 is efficient for general enterprise workloads, relational databases, distributed caching layers, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine in the DAv4 series powered by a 16-core AMD EPYC 7452 processor delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs at 3.525 GHz. It is provisioned with 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, and includes 859 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark results place its single-core stress-ng performance in the top 25 percent and its PassMark memory subsystem throughput in the top 10 percent, despite multi-core compute scoring in the mid-range. While the architecture lacks AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU acceleration, it provides strong baseline execution for integer, cryptographic, and memory-intensive operations. These hardware parameters make the instance suitable for mid-to-large relational databases, caching tiers running Redis, multi-threaded software compilation, and scalable enterprise web backends requiring balanced compute and fast local scratch storage.
